content.text: {"decision": "explain", "likely_cause": "Likely cause: On item:list, the Item 190 scroll container has no visible way to reach a target row quickly, so users scroll down and back up in repeated passes with no clicks in between, then click Item 190 near the top of the list.", "fix": "Fix: On the item:list screen, add a search or filter input above the Item 190 list container so users can jump to the target row, and check that the pointer region at about (1275, 400) inside that container is not a non-interactive element that users are trying to use as a scroll handle.", "cited_event_ids": ["54", "55", "57", "59", "60", "62", "64", "66", "70", "56:60", "61:65", "63:68", "67:72", "339", "341", "342", "344", "346", "348", "350", "351", "356"], "confidence": "med", "unsupported": ["The user's intent for the scroll reversals is not observable; the search-field cause is an inference from the repeated reversals before a click.", "The scroll_y values are absolute positions in the windows; the reversal direction is derived from the sequence, not from a direction field.", "What lies at pointer position (1275, 400) is not stated in the events; the label is only Item 190 with tag div.", "Whether the list has a search or filter control today is not in the events.", "Whether the target item was the one clicked at the end, or what the report screen needed, is not verified.", "Dropped pointer samples (83, 102, 110) mean pointer paths are incomplete.", "No abandonment is observed, so the cost of the behaviour is limited to the 8.5 s median time lost in the insight."]}
